text: Axial nozzle thrust F = mdot*Ve + (pe-pa)*Ae. mdot is mass flow in kg/s, Ve exit velocity in m/s, pe exit static pressure and pa ambient pressure in Pa, Ae exit area in m^2. Both terms have units N. Pressure thrust can be positive, zero, or negative. Do not omit it merely because exhaust velocity is given.

For steady one-dimensional calorically perfect ideal gas with a choked sonic throat, mdot = p0*At/sqrt(T0)*sqrt(gamma/R)*(2/(gamma+1))^((gamma+1)/(2*(gamma-1))). p0 and T0 are stagnation conditions in Pa and K, At is throat area in m^2, R is specific gas constant in J/(kg*K), gamma>1. This choked formula requires throat Mach number 1.

The ideal isentropic area-Mach relation is Ae/At = (1/Me)*[(2/(gamma+1))*(1+(gamma-1)*Me^2/2)]^((gamma+1)/(2*(gamma-1))). Ratios greater than 1 have subsonic and supersonic roots. A stated shock-free supersonic nozzle requires Me>1. At the sonic throat the ratio is 1.

For constant-gamma isentropic ideal flow, Te=T0/(1+(gamma-1)*Me^2/2), pe=p0*(Te/T0)^(gamma/(gamma-1)), and Ve=Me*sqrt(gamma*R*Te). These use exit static temperature and pressure, not chamber stagnation quantities in their place. If area ratio is supplied, determine the correct Mach branch first.

Use coherent SI units in products: 1 kPa=1000 Pa, 1 MPa=1000000 Pa, 1 cm^2=0.0001 m^2, 1 g/s=0.001 kg/s, 1 km/s=1000 m/s, 1 kN=1000 N. Convert area as a squared length. A numerical answer needs a dimensionally compatible unit.

A single shock-free constant-gamma isentropic model has a restricted domain. An internal normal shock breaks isentropic evolution across the whole nozzle. Strongly changing specific heats invalidate a single constant gamma. A subsonic unchoked throat invalidates the sonic-throat choked mass-flow formula. A request that insists on these incompatible assumptions requires abstention with the specific issue. This is an applicability rubric for this benchmark, not a general prohibition on solving such flows with richer models.

Missing required inputs prevent a unique numerical answer. Supplied-state thrust needs mdot, Ve, pe, pa and Ae unless a term is explicitly specified as zero. Choked mass flow needs p0, T0, At, gamma and R. Exit speed from area ratio needs T0, gamma, R and the stated branch. Do not assume standard air properties or atmospheric pressure when the question forbids assumptions.

Mass continuity requires mdot=rho_e*Ve*Ae with rho_e=pe/(R*Te). The ideal formula ignores viscous loss, heat transfer, multidimensional effects, separation, variable chemistry and combustion dynamics. An ideal reference can test computational consistency without validating a real rocket engine.
